title: test: cover the wrapper self-restart hand-over in both postflight harnesses
description:
FOLLOW-UP to df42861 (governor fix, 2026-09-18). The wrapper self-restart — the top-of-loop check that relaunches when the wrapper's own bytes change on disk — has NO harness or parity coverage in either twin. `grep -n 'source changed on disk' scripts/tests/*` returns nothing today.

That gap let a real defect live: the ps1 path relaunched via `Start-Process`, which gave the new wrapper its own console window and left the launching terminal at a prompt. Operators read that as a dead seat and relaunched the same worker id, so two wrapper loops shared one seat and two CLIs reviewed task-49ec8755 at the same time (2026-09-18, qa-a36819c3 and worker-d0c3b06e). df42861 hands over with the call operator instead, past the outer finally, and deregisters with reason `wrapper_restart` first, matching the sh twin's `exec`.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE CARD: scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1} were held by task-e47284ef when the fix landed, and task-32ecce5d has the same files next. Adding the case then would have been swept into another task's commit.

WHAT TO ASSERT (daemon-free, in the existing fake-proxy harness): with the wrapper copy's bytes changed between iterations, the run must show exactly one `deregister_worker` RPC carrying reason `wrapper_restart`, then a fresh registration from the relaunched wrapper, and exactly one restart per on-disk change (the relaunched process re-reads the hash and must not thrash). The engine difference is the hand-over mechanism itself, so assert what both twins share — the RPC sequence — rather than pids. On ps1 the relaunch is a child of the wrapper and inherits its console; on sh `exec` replaces the process, so the pid is unchanged.

SUGGESTED PROOF (the worker decides): revert the call operator to `Start-Process` in a scratch copy and show the case turns red, the same way the other harness mutations are proven.
definitionOfDone: Both scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 gain a self-restart case: change the wrapper copy's bytes between iterations and assert one deregister_worker with reason 'wrapper_restart', a fresh registration afterwards, and exactly one restart per on-disk change.
The case is proven RED on a scratch copy that restores the pre-df42861 behaviour (Start-Process relaunch, deregister reason terminal_closed).
MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and the ps1 twin both pass on a quiet box, and parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 stay green.
Any new banner or reason literal is registered in both parity checkers' fixed lists.
taskRails: Harness-only change; scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh stay as df42861 left them unless the case proves them wrong.
Keep both harness twins byte-identical in the shared fake-proxy JavaScript, as the surrounding cases already require.

amendments.description:
RED FIRST (sh harness only). Add a daemon-free, git-free self-restart case to scripts/tests/postflight.sh after the heartbeat-sidecar checks: after the `fi` that closes the `count_after_wait` check, and before `# --- Quality gate (settings.qualityGate)`. Find the spot by these anchors, never by line numbers; task-84150869 and task-07474ee4 edit this file first.

(1) Shared sequence script. Step 3 writes the SAME bytes into postflight.ps1:
cat > "$TMP_DIR/restart-sequence.cjs" <<'JS'
// Self-restart RPC sequence, byte-identical in postflight.sh and postflight.ps1:
// c = claim_next_task (the daemon re-registers a worker on its claim), r = this
// seat's deregister_worker with reason wrapper_restart, x = any other deregister.
// The last line may still be mid-append, so an unparsable line is skipped.
const fs=require('fs'),[file,worker]=process.argv.slice(2);
const text=fs.existsSync(file)?fs.readFileSync(file,'utf8'):'';
const rows=text.split('\n').flatMap(l=>{try{return [JSON.parse(l)];}catch(e){return [];}});
process.stdout.write(rows.map(r=>r.tool==='claim_next_task'?'c':r.tool!=='deregister_worker'?'':
  r.args&&r.args.workerId===worker&&r.args.reason==='wrapper_restart'?'r':'x').join(''));
JS
It reads <project>/.moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl. The fake proxy already logs every claim_next_task and deregister_worker there in call order, so it does NOT change.

(2) Fixture:
- mkdir "$TMP_DIR/self-restart" and cp -R "$ROOT_DIR/scripts" into it. The restart deregisters through the sibling moe-call.sh.
- chmod +x the copied moe-agent.sh; exec needs it.
- A project dir holding .moe/project.json {"settings":{"autoCommit":false}}, an empty .moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl, and .moe/daemon.json. moe-call.sh refuses to run without daemon.json.
- No git.

(3) Launch the COPY in the background by its absolute path, with the heartbeat case's env shape:
PATH="$TMP_DIR:$PATH" HOME="$HOME_DIR" MOE_PROXY_PATH="$FAKE_PROXY" FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1 <copy> --project <proj> --worker-id worker-self-restart --role worker --no-start-daemon --command /bin/true --loop --poll-interval 1 >"$TMP_DIR/self-restart.out" 2>&1 &
Add the pid to LIVE_PIDS at once. Restore LIVE_PIDS after the case kills it, because the pid can be reused.

(4) Three stages. Each has a deadline of $POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC (measured with $SECONDS) and polls every 0.5 s. EVERY poll fails at once if:
- the sequence contains x (the hand-over took an exit path);
- the count of r exceeds the changes made so far (thrash);
- kill -0 says the wrapper is gone.
The stages:
 a) wait for ^c;
 b) printf '\n# self-restart probe 1\n' >> <copy>, then wait for ^c+rcc;
 c) printf '\n# self-restart probe 2\n' >> <copy>, then wait for ^c+rc{2,}rcc.
Append only. The file ends with the main loop's `done`, which bash has already parsed, and exec re-reads the whole file. Keep each regex in a variable for [[ =~ ]].

(5) Snapshot the sequence, then kill -KILL the wrapper and `wait ... || true`. Assert:
- the snapshot matches ^c+rc{2,}rc{2,}$;
- self-restart.out has exactly 2 lines 'wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it' (grep -Fc ... || true, because grep -c exits 1 on zero matches under set -e).

(6) Error handling:
- A failure helper kills the wrapper, prints the output file and .moe/deregister.log to stderr, then `SELF-RESTART FAILED: <why> (sequence: <seq>)`, then exits 1.
- Every wait is bounded. An abort under set -e still reaches the EXIT trap, which kills LIVE_PIDS.
- Echo '[self-restart] a changed wrapper restarts once per change and re-registers' at the start and '[self-restart] ok' at the end.
- Never print a line starting with SKIP: CI's postflight-safe.mjs fails the run on one.
- Leave SCOPE_SCENARIOS_RUN alone.

(7) RED on the pre-fix wrapper. The fix already landed as 45633c7, so restore the old capture in a SCRATCH copy only.
- Build a subset harness by anchors (mem:pattern-postflight-red-proof-via-temp-tree): [0, `FROZEN_SUITE=`) + this case + `echo "PASS postflight.sh"`. Put it in D:/moe-scratch/<unique>/scripts/tests/ beside a copy of scripts/, so ROOT_DIR is the scratch root.
- Then `git show 45633c7^:scripts/moe-agent.sh > <scratch>/scripts/moe-agent.sh`. If 07474ee4 has since changed that file, move the capture back below the hash by hand instead.
- Expected: FAIL with 'the wrapper exited', sequence cr, and output showing 'Error: Provide --project or --project-name'.
- Architect pre-validation on Git Bash, same stage logic: pre-fix cr then exit; fixed crccrcc with 2 banners; S1 cx; S2 r.
Paste your failure lines into the step note.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX the sh self-restart argv in scripts/moe-agent.sh. This is the only wrapper edit. The task rail allows it because the step-1 case proves the wrapper wrong, and the human approved fixing it in this task (architect REPL, 2026-09-19; see the task comment).

ROOT CAUSE. `MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV=("$@")` sits beside the restart hash capture. That is long after the top-level option parser (`while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case $1 in ... shift`) has consumed every positional parameter, so the array is ALWAYS empty. The restart then runs `exec "$MOE_WRAPPER_PATH"` with no arguments. The relaunched process exits 1 with 'Error: Provide --project or --project-name', and by then the old process has already deregistered: every sh seat dies on its first hot reload. Broken since a0646b3 (2026-08-18); reproduced in a scratch copy on 2026-09-19.

CHANGE:
- Move the capture to just above `# Parse arguments` (before that while loop). Give it a comment saying why: the parser shifts every argument away, and the self-restart must re-exec with the launch argv.
- Delete the late `MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV=("$@")`.
- Leave MOE_WRAPPER_PATH, the hash capture and the whole restart block byte-for-byte as they are. No other edit.
- ps1 is unaffected: its relaunch reads the process command line (df42861) or @PSBoundParameters (84150869).
- Error handling is unchanged: the fail-open hash capture and the 'wrapper relaunch failed; continuing on current bytes' fallback stay as they are.

VERIFY:
(a) bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh.
(b) The step-1 subset harness PASSES on a fresh scratch copy of the FIXED scripts/.
(c) Mutants of the fixed wrapper, each in its own scratch copy. Never touch the live file: live sh seats hash it.
  - S1: the restart deregister's reason spelled terminal_closed. Expect a FAIL naming x.
  - S2: the launch-hash capture hashes /dev/null instead of $MOE_WRAPPER_PATH, so every check restarts. Expect a FAIL for a restart with no change behind it.
  Run the unmutated control first and last.
(d) bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh still passes.
Paste every verdict line into the step note.

OPERATIONAL NOTE for the completion summary: any sh seat still running the old bytes dies once more on the reload this landing itself triggers, because its captured argv is empty. Relaunch sh seats once after this lands.

implementationPlan.description:
ps1 TWIN, built on task-84150869's design (dependsOn guarantees it is DONE). Its approved plan added a hot-reload arm to scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, 'hot reload keeps one wrapper process'.
- The arm runs a copy of scripts/ with -Loop -PollInterval 1, FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle and MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1, and appends a comment twice.
- It asserts: 2 wrapper_restart deregisters; exactly 1 wrapper process after each reload; one runner identity across all claims; and a claim after the second reload.
Find it with grep -n wrapper_restart. EXTEND that arm; do not add a second one, and keep all of its assertions.

(1) Write restart-sequence.cjs into $tempRoot with the SAME bytes as step 1: Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 of a single-quoted here-string, as $fakeProxy is written (node strips the PS 5.1 BOM). Call it as "$(& node $restartSeq $rpcLog '<the arm's worker id>')"; the string cast turns empty output into ''.

(2) Drive the arm's waits with the same three stages, regexes and fail-fast checks as the sh twin:
- 'wrapper gone' is $p.HasExited;
- the second reload also waits for the second quiet claim (^c+rc{2,}rcc) before the arm stops the tree;
- keep the arm's per-reload process count after each stage's wait;
- snapshot and assert ^c+rc{2,}rc{2,}$ BEFORE the stop;
- after the stop, assert exactly 2 'wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it' lines in the captured output.
Error handling:
- retry each append on an IOException, up to 20 x 100 ms: Get-FileHash holds a read-share lock while the wrapper hashes itself;
- a failed stage throws 'SELF-RESTART FAILED: <why> (sequence: <seq>)' after printing the captured output and deregister.log.

(3) In the arm's finally, after its taskkill /T /F, Stop-Process -Force every process whose CommandLine contains the COPIED wrapper's full path (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, IndexOf with OrdinalIgnoreCase). Otherwise a relaunch that escaped the tree, like the mutant below, idle-loops forever. Match ONLY that unique temp path, never 'moe-agent.ps1', which would kill live fleet seats.

(4) FALLBACK if the arm does not exist (84150869 dropped or re-planned it): add the ps1 twin of the step-1 case after the heartbeat case, with the same fixture, stages and checks.
- Launch: Start-Process $psExe -NoProfile -File <copy> ... -Loop -PollInterval 1 -PassThru -NoNewWindow, output redirected.
- Stop: taskkill /T /F, plus the sweep.

(5) RED PROOF (DoD 2: the literal pre-df42861 behaviour), in a scratch copy of scripts/.
- In the copy's moe-agent.ps1 restart check (anchor: Write-Host "wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it"), replace `Invoke-MoeDeregister -Reason 'wrapper_restart'` and the line that requests the hand-over (84150869's reload flag) with:
  `Start-Process -FilePath (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path -ArgumentList @([Environment]::GetCommandLineArgs() | Select-Object -Skip 1) -WorkingDirectory (Get-Location).Path | Out-Null`
  and keep `break`. The exit path then deregisters with its default reason, terminal_closed, exactly as before df42861.
- Run the scratch postflight.ps1 under pwsh 7 AND PS 5.1, launched from PowerShell, never from Git Bash. Use the full harness (about 7 min per engine) or an anchor subset.
- Expect the arm to FAIL with a sequence showing x and no r.
- Confirm no process whose CommandLine contains the scratch path survives the run.
- The unmutated control must PASS.
Paste both engines' failure lines into the step note. Applying S1/S2 to the ps1 copy is optional.

PARITY (DoD 4): register in both parity checkers the literals the cases assert.

scripts/tests/parity-check.sh, after the runner-reattach prose loop:
  # Self-restart hand-over: the banner an operator sees and the deregister reason
  # the postflight self-restart cases assert, spelled identically in both.
  for lit in 'wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it' wrapper_restart; do

scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1: add 'self-restart' = @('wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it', 'wrapper_restart') to $required, with the same comment.

Both literals are already in both wrappers, so both checkers still PASS. The checkers' existing error handling (collect every failure, exit 1) is reused unchanged.

BITE CHECK: in a scratch copy of scripts/, rename wrapper_restart in the copied moe-agent.sh ONLY. parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 (pwsh), run from that scratch root, must both FAIL and name it. Paste both lines.

terminal_closed is not asserted by any case, so it is not registered (YAGNI).

VERIFY sequentially, on a quiet box (mem:moes-test-env-quirks). Nothing runs concurrently with a harness.
1. bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh, pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1 and powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1: all PASS.
2. From the PowerShell tool, set $env:MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC='180', then run pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, then powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/postflight.ps1: PASS postflight.ps1 on both engines.
3. MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh: PASS postflight.sh. It takes about 40-50 min on this box, so start it with run_in_background and block on a bounded poller, never a foreground sleep.
4. Byte identity: extract restart-sequence.cjs and the fake-proxy JS from both harnesses and cmp each pair (both harness files are LF).
5. Wrapper and diff scope:
   - git diff --quiet -- scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (the ps1 wrapper is untouched);
   - git diff -- scripts/moe-agent.sh shows only the moved argv capture and its comment;
   - git diff --stat lists only the five planned files plus this task's .moe record.
6. A PRE-EXISTING frozen loop arm can flake at 180 under load. If one does, rerun that arm alone (MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY=<arm>) and record it. Only a red self-restart case counts against this change.

complete_task verification: the full postflight.sh command, with its PASS line as outputTail. Name the ps1 and parity results, and the sh relaunch note from step 2, in the summary.

SELF-REVIEW, posted as a task comment:
1. Can two harness runs collide? Temp roots are unique, and the ps1 sweep matches only the unique copied path.
2. Can the case pass vacuously? No: every stage needs an observed c or r. A wrapper whose restart is inert (for example an empty launch hash) times out at stage b.
3. Error handling: are thrash, a missing restart, an exit-path hand-over and a dead relaunch each reported with a distinct message, and is every wait bounded?
4. Does anything leak? Check the LIVE_PIDS window on sh, the finally sweep on ps1, and that nothing is written outside TMP_DIR / $tempRoot.
5. Platforms: Linux CI (exec keeps the pid), Git Bash (MSYS exec), PS 5.1 and 7, and no SKIP-prefixed lines. On stock macOS without sha256sum the wrapper's reload is off by design (fail-open), so the sh case fails there; CI runs postflight.sh on Linux only. Note this; do not fix it here.
6. Is the new shared JS byte-identical in both harnesses, the fake proxy untouched, parity updated in both checkers, and the wrapper diff only the argv move?
7. Would the case have caught both incidents? ps1: yes, it goes red on the pre-df42861 proof. sh: yes, it goes red on the real argv bug. The console-window symptom itself is invisible to RPCs; 84150869's process-count and identity checks cover that side.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A frozen-suite mode (JS shared by both harnesses): rejected. Every frozen mode builds a git fixture plus a gate, and its KILL_ON_MARKER supervisor only kills; this case needs no git and staged edits between iterations.
- A second ps1 arm beside task-84150869's hot-reload arm: rejected. It would duplicate the copy/spawn/kill machinery; instead extend that arm with the shared RPC-sequence assertion (governor note: plan against its design).
- Asserting pids or runner identity: rejected, per the task. sh exec keeps the pid, and 84150869's design decides identity on ps1. The RPC sequence is what both twins share.
- Logging join_team/chat_join in the fake proxy as the 'fresh registration' marker: rejected. It would change the byte-identical fake proxy and every evidence-rpcs consumer. claim_next_task auto-registers the worker (claimNextTask.ts, 'Auto-register or update worker entity'), so the first claim after the deregister IS the re-registration.
- A literal 'pre-df42861' red proof for sh: impossible, because sh always exec'd with wrapper_restart. The human chose the real argv bug plus mutants S1/S2 instead.
- Filing the sh argv bug as a separate card: the human chose to fix it here (a one-line move; the rail allows wrapper edits the case proves wrong).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- sh restart block: at the top of `while [ "$LOOP_RUNNING" = true ]` in moe-agent.sh. The hash is captured once before the loop (sha256sum, fail-open to ''). On a change it prints the banner, runs stop_heartbeat_sidecar, deregisters via `bash $SCRIPT_DIR/moe-call.sh deregister_worker` with reason wrapper_restart (moe-call.sh needs <project>/.moe/daemon.json), removes SECURE_TEMP_DIR, then `exec "$MOE_WRAPPER_PATH" "${MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV[@]}"`. MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV is captured AFTER the option parser shifted everything away, so it is empty. That is the bug: the relaunch prints 'Error: Provide --project or --project-name' and exits 1.
- ps1 restart check: at the top of the do-loop, `Invoke-MoeDeregister -Reason 'wrapper_restart'` then break. The hand-over is df42861's call operator at the file bottom, and 84150869 turns it into an in-process supervisor rerun. Either way the RPC sequence is the same.
- The EXIT trap (sh) and the default Invoke-MoeDeregister reason (ps1) are both 'terminal_closed', the reason the pre-df42861 restart posted.
- The fake proxy appends claim_next_task and deregister_worker rows to .moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl in call order; deregister rows also go to deregister.log. FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle answers hasNext:false, and a --loop wrapper then launches no CLI and polls again.
- moe-agent.sh ends with the main loop's `done`, so appended bytes are never executed by the running bash.
- CI runs postflight.sh on Linux only and postflight.ps1 on Windows (powershell and pwsh), both via postflight-safe.mjs (20-minute cap). Any output line starting with SKIP fails the run; lastScenario only parses single-letter [scenario X].
- Harness files are LF, so the shared JS can be compared byte-exact.
planningNotes.risks:
- Mutate ONLY scratch copies (D:/moe-scratch/<unique>/scripts). Live seats hash their launcher, and an edit to the repo file reloads them.
- The ps1 process sweep must match the unique copied path only; a broader match kills live fleet seats.
- sh LIVE_PIDS: restore it after the kill, because the pid can be reused.
- Get-FileHash holds a read-share lock, so retry ps1 appends on IOException.
- The pre-df42861 mutant opens a console window and orphans its child; the sweep kills it.
